passage:
Dear Mr. Reynolds,

I am writing to sincerely apologize for my behavior during last Friday's team meeting. After reflecting on the situation, I realize that my actions were unprofessional and did not align with the standards expected in our workplace.

At the time, I was feeling overwhelmed by multiple deadlines and underestimated how stressed I had become. When my proposal was questioned, I reacted defensively and spoke out of turn. Raising my voice and interrupting colleagues was inappropriate, regardless of the pressure I was under. I understand now that this disrupted the meeting and made others uncomfortable.

Over the weekend, I took time to reflect on the incident and review our company's code of conduct. It became clear that professionalism involves managing emotions, especially during disagreements. While constructive debate is encouraged, it must always remain respectful and solution-focused. I regret allowing my frustration to overshadow these principles.

I have already taken steps to ensure this does not happen again. I have enrolled in a workplace communication workshop offered by the company and have started using stress-management strategies to better handle demanding situations. Additionally, I reached out individually to the team members involved to apologize and listen to their perspectives.

I value my role within the organization and the trust placed in me. This incident has been a wake-up call, reminding me that technical skills alone are not enough; professionalism and emotional intelligence are equally important. I am committed to rebuilding confidence through consistent, respectful behavior moving forward.

Thank you for taking the time to read this message. I appreciate your understanding and the opportunity to learn from this mistake.

Sincerely,
Marcus Lee
